description: We are a small group of friends from University of Mauritius who like to take on hard challenges. We are not the sharpest tool in the shed but we persevere through it.
summary:
We built A.R.E.S. Med (Astronaut Rapid Evaluation Support & Medical System), an autonomous, closed-loop clinical monitoring and triage console for deep-space exploration. The system integrates an onboard physiological digital twin with an edge anomaly detector (using JPL Power-of-Ten safety rules and cosmic-ray single-event upset filtering), an offline clinical decision support engine grounded in NASA standards (NASA-STD-3001, CHeCS), and an interactive mission dashboard featuring a 3D anatomical body HUD and real-time biometric telemetry.

How it addresses the challenge:
On deep-space transit to the Moon or Mars, round-trip radio latency to Earth reaches up to 40 minutes, rendering real-time guidance from terrestrial flight surgeons impossible during acute crises. A.R.E.S. Med operates 100% locally and offline. It continuously evaluates crew vitals against spaceflight-adapted baselines, recommends protocol-driven treatments for recognized conditions, enforces certified abstention with drug lockouts on novel zero-day anomalies to eliminate AI hallucinations, and dynamically simulates closed-loop recovery.

Deep-space exploration shifts astronaut healthcare from Earth reliance to onboard autonomy. A.R.E.S. Med mitigates mission-critical risks,such as CO₂ toxicity, cardiac arrhythmias, and radiation exposure,empowering crew members to make rapid, verified, life-saving clinical decisions without waiting for ground control.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

A.R.E.S. Med (Astronaut Rapid Evaluation Support & Medical System) is an autonomous, closed-loop clinical monitoring and decision support system engineered for deep-space transit. Operating 100% locally and offline, it works across four integrated layers:

  • Physiological Digital Twin (Autonomous Astronaut Agent): Dynamically simulates 1Hz biometric telemetry (heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂, HRV, core temperature) and microgravity state machines (sleep, resting, exercise, EVA) for crew member Cmdr. Alex Vance, modulated by real NASA DONKI space weather solar radiation feeds.
    • Mode A (Confidence ≥ 75%): Delivers verified NASA clinical guidelines, CHeCS medication dosages, and explicit contraindication warnings.
    • Mode B (Novel Zero-Day Anomaly < 75%): Enforces Certified Abstention (zero hallucinations), initiates emergency ABC stabilization protocols, orders point-of-care diagnostics (i-STAT, ultrasound), locks out high-risk drugs, and packages telemetry for prioritized Earth transmission.
  • Mission Control Console & 3D Holographic HUD: A dark-mode mission dashboard providing real-time telemetry charting, an interactive 3D anatomical model highlighting affected organ systems (SANS-01, CV-02, ECLSS-03, RAD-04), and a dynamic treatment recovery loop where applying treatments restores vitals tick-by-tick.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Zero Dependence on Earth Uplink: Astronauts receive instant, life-saving triage during communications blackouts or communication delays up to 20 minutes each way.
  • Safety-First AI with Anti-Hallucination Guardrails: Unlike generic generative AI models that risk hallucinating treatments in high-stakes environments, our certified abstention threshold and automated contraindication lockouts prevent medical errors (e.g., locking out opioids during elevated cabin CO₂).
  • Noise and Bit-Flip Resilience: Edge debouncing ensures that spacecraft radiation hardware anomalies do not trigger false alarms.
  • Full Accountability & Earth Synchronization: Generates and queues clinical incident PDF reports and automated email packets ready for transmission to ground control once telemetry syncs.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

A.R.E.S. Med bridges the critical capability gap for NASA’s upcoming Artemis lunar missions and Mars transit. By transforming astronaut medical care from Earth-supervised telemetry to onboard autonomous clinical triage, it directly preserves crew survival, prevents mission aborts, and sets a benchmark for resilient, edge-deployed clinical software.

4. Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used:

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn (REST & live /ws/telemetry WebSockets), Pydantic v2, HTTPX, ReportLab (automated clinical PDF generation).
  • Frontend: Modern Vanilla JavaScript (ES modules), HTML5, Custom Dark-Mode CSS3, Chart.js (rolling biometric telemetry).
  • 3D Visualization: Three.js, WebGL, custom Blender-modeled anatomical astronaut hologram (.glb).
  • Data & NASA Standards: NASA-STD-3001 (Vols 1 & 2), NASA Space Flight Human-System Standard, NASA Space Weather DONKI API, NASA CHeCS formulary, JPL Institutional Coding Standard (Power-of-Ten rules).
  • Testing & Tools: Pytest, Node test runner, Git/GitHub.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Closed-Loop Physiological Recovery: Rather than merely displaying alerts, A.R.E.S. Med is closed-loop: administering oxygen or IV fluids actively models the physiological recovery curve in the digital twin, returning vitals to baseline in real time.
  • 3D Spatial Medical Awareness: Replacing text-heavy medical logs with a glowing 3D anatomical avatar allows non-physician astronauts under high cognitive load to immediately visualize affected physiological systems.
  • Certified Abstention Architecture: Instead of forcing answers on ambiguous data, the AI safely steps back into protocol-driven stabilization, turning standard AI limitations into a certified safety feature.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Deep-Space Communication Constraints: Designed strictly offline-first to withstand the 20-minute one-way radio propagation delay to Mars.
  • Microgravity Physiology: Incorporated cephalic fluid shifts, spaceflight-adapted cardiovascular baselines, Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), and circadian rhythm desynchronization.
  • Space Radiation & Hardware Failures: Factored in deep-space galactic cosmic rays causing hardware bit-flips, implementing debouncing algorithms to verify data integrity before clinical decisions are made.
  • Cognitive Load & Crew Stress: Designed high-contrast, clutter-free HUD elements so compromised or stressed crew members can execute critical emergency actions with single-click verifications.
